key_insight: Biomedical reranking meaningfully improved retrieval of the right evidence from long clinical notes, but answer quality improved only modestly.
clinical_relevance: For longitudinal patient-question answering, better evidence selection can help surface the most relevant chart fragments within tight context limits.
method: Built a retrieval-augmented QA pipeline for longitudinal clinical notes
Combined PubMedBERT dense retrieval, BM25, weighted reciprocal-rank fusion, and MedCPT cross-encoder reranking
Compared retrieval and answer performance with and without reranking
evidence_signal: On 1,000 question-answer pairs from 200 bariatric surgery patients, reranking raised Hit@10 from 46.6% to 60.6% and mean reciprocal rank from 0.2371 to 0.3252; judged answer correctness increased from 44.8% to 48.6%.
watch_item: Retrieval gains did not translate proportionally into answer correctness, so deployment still depends on model generation quality and context-window constraints.
paper_title: Evaluating Biomedical Reranking for LLM-Based Question Answering over Longitudinal Clinical Notes
